northern.name: Northern Zone
northern.bounds: East of the Connecticut River Zone and north of the Inland Zone, beginning at the junction of Rte. 10 and Rte. 25A in Orford, east on Rte. 25A to Rte. 25 in Wentworth, southeast on Rte. 25 to Exit 26 off I-93 in Plymouth, south on I-93 to Rte. 3 at Exit 24 in Ashland, northeast on Rte. 3 to Rte. 113 in Holderness, north on Rte. 113 to Rte. 113-A in Sandwich, north on Rte. 113-A to Rte. 113 in Tamworth, east on Rte. 113 to Rte. 16 in Chocorua, north on Rte. 16 to Rte. 302 in Conway, east on Rte. 302 to the ME–NH border.

inland.name: Inland Zone
inland.bounds: Area of the state east of the Connecticut River Zone, south of the Northern Zone, and west of the Coastal Zone.

coastal.name: Coastal Zone
coastal.bounds: Beginning at the Maine–New Hampshire line in Rollinsford, that portion of the state east of a boundary formed by Route 4 west to the city of Dover, south to the intersection of Route 108 through Madbury, Durham and Newmarket to the junction of Route 85 in Newfields, south to Route 101 in Exeter, east to Interstate 95 in Hampton, and south to the Massachusetts line.

ct.name: Connecticut River Zone
ct.bounds: The New Hampshire portion is the area west of Rte. 63 at the MA border, north on Rte. 63 to Rte. 12, north on Rte. 12 to Rte. 12-A, north on Rte. 12A to Rte. 10, north on Rte. 10 to Rte. 135, north on Rte. 135 to Rte. 3, north on Rte. 3 to the intersection with the Connecticut River. The zone also covers the Vermont side east of I-91, Rte. 2, Rte. 102 and Rte. 253 north to Canada.
ct.note: New Hampshire Inland Zone regulations apply to the entire Connecticut River Zone in both New Hampshire and Vermont. The two states have enacted reciprocal migratory waterfowl hunting rights for licensed hunters in this zone.

bags.detail: Within the 6-duck daily limit: no more than 4 mallards, of which no more than 2 may be hens; 2 black ducks; 3 wood ducks; 3 pintail; 2 canvasbacks; 2 redheads; 1 scaup; and no more than 3 each of scoters, long-tailed ducks or eiders, of which only 1 eider may be a hen. The season on harlequin duck is closed. Possession is three times the daily limit.
The 5-merganser daily limit is in addition to the 6-duck daily limit.
Sea ducks count toward the general duck bag limit in all zones. Species: common eider, surf scoter, white-winged scoter, black scoter, long-tailed duck, bufflehead and common goldeneye.
Regular season, same dates as ducks.
HIP certification required. No state waterfowl licence or federal duck stamp needed.
No HIP, state migratory licence or federal duck stamp required.

rules.d: Waterfowl, woodcock and snipe: one-half hour before sunrise to sunset. Crow: one-half hour before sunrise to one-half hour after sunset.
Nontoxic shot is required for all waterfowl. It is illegal to possess any shotgun shell containing lead shot while hunting migratory waterfowl. This does not apply to woodcock or snipe.

No shotgun larger than 10 gauge. The gun must be plugged so it holds no more than three shells total — two in the magazine plus one in the chamber. Air rifles may not be used for migratory game birds. Bow and arrow is legal.
Electronic calls may be used for crows, and during the special September Canada goose season only.
You may not carry a loaded firearm in a motorboat under power, and you may not hunt from a motorboat or sailboat until all forward motion has ceased.
RSA 207:7 V allows shooting injured or crippled waterfowl from a motorized watercraft while in the sea duck hunting area. That exception applies nowhere else.
All coastal waters, plus the waters of rivers and streams seaward from the first upstream bridge from the coast.
Placing bait, or hunting over a baited area, is prohibited.
Selling mounted migratory game birds is prohibited under 50 CFR 20.91(b).
NH Fish and Game advises caution when field dressing ducks: wear gloves, work in a ventilated area, wash up afterwards, and do not handle birds that appear sick.

New Hampshire Inland Zone regulations apply to the entire Connecticut River Zone in both New Hampshire and Vermont. The two states have reciprocal migratory waterfowl hunting rights for licensed hunters in this zone.

January 23–24, 2027, for hunters licensed in New Hampshire. Participants may hunt the Connecticut River Zone but must launch from New Hampshire. Carry proof of eligibility: an active, retired or National Guard/Reservist ID, a NH driver licence with veteran status, or a DD214 or DD215.

September 26–27, 2026, statewide, for hunters 15 and younger. No licence is required under 16, but the youth must be accompanied by an adult 18 or older holding a current hunting licence. The adult may not take waterfowl.

licences.d: Residents: a current Regular NH Hunting, Combination or Archery licence. Nonresidents: a Regular NH Hunting, Combination, Archery or Small Game licence.
Required to hunt ducks and geese.
Free. Call 1-800-207-6183 or get it through huntnh.com, then write the number on your hunting licence.
Signed across the face, or the electronic version. Sold at many U.S. Post Offices and at duckstamp.com.
No licence required, but must be accompanied by a properly licensed adult 18 or older.
